The average distance from the Earth to the Sun is approximately 149.6 million kilometers (about 92.96 million miles). This distance is defined as one Astronomical Unit (AU) and is used as a standard unit of measurement in astronomy. However, it's important to note that Earth's distance from the Sun varies throughout the year because Earth's orbit is elliptical. The closest approach (perihelion) is around 147.1 million kilometers, and the farthest point (aphelion) is around 152.1 million kilometers.

This variation is relatively small but has implications for the amount of solar radiation Earth receives at different times of the year.
